# Project Prompt and Commands

## Prompt

> Set up a minimal Express 5 backend using TypeScript, NodeNext ESM, strict mode, and tsx. Create dev, typecheck, build, and start scripts. Explain the generated files and verify each command.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm run dev
```

The original prompt also requires the production-style start command:

```bash
npm start
```

## Generated files

- `package.json`: Declares ESM mode, dependencies, and the four npm scripts.
- `package-lock.json`: Locks the exact dependency tree for reproducible installs.
- `.gitignore`: Keeps installed dependencies and generated build output out of Git.
- `tsconfig.json`: Enables strict TypeScript and NodeNext ESM compilation from `src` to `dist`.
- `src/server.ts`: Starts Express 5 and exposes `GET /`, which returns a JSON greeting.
- `dist/server.js`: Generated by `npm run build`; this is the file executed by `npm start`.

## Script behavior

- `npm run typecheck`: Checks all TypeScript types without writing output files.
- `npm run build`: Compiles `src/server.ts` into `dist/server.js`.
- `npm run dev`: Runs the TypeScript source with tsx in watch mode for development.
- `npm start`: Runs the compiled JavaScript with Node.js.

## Verification

Verified with Node.js `v22.19.0` and npm `10.9.3`:

- `npm run typecheck` passed and did not create `dist`.
- `npm run build` passed and created `dist/server.js`.
- `npm run dev` started the tsx watcher on port `3101`; `GET /` returned `{"message":"Hello from Express 5 with TypeScript!"}`.
- `npm start` ran `node dist/server.js` on port `3102`; `GET /` returned the same JSON response.

The temporary verification servers were stopped after their HTTP responses were confirmed.
